title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — July 2026
description: This week, three IPOs — Xtranet Technologies, INDO-MIM, and Lohia Corp — are closing today, July 27th. Propshop Events and Exhibitions' IPO opens today, July .

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your demat and trading account, usually via your bank's net banking portal using the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility, or through your stockbroker's platform.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must bid for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer shares than the specified lot size.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME (Small and Medium Enterprises) IPOs are for smaller companies and are listed on dedicated SME platforms (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME) with different regulatory requirements and often higher minimum investment amounts.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you don't receive an allotment of shares, the money you had blocked for the IPO application will be unblocked and released back into your bank account, usually within a few days after the allotment finalisation.

faq.q: Can I sell my shares on the listing day?
faq.a: Yes, once your allotted shares are credited to your demat account and the company officially lists on the stock exchange, you are free to sell them on the listing day itself, just like any other stock.
